CXI.A: Functions are small and flat; almost no branching-heavy code.
CXI.B: Mostly easy functions with a few branching-heavy spots.
CXI.C: A meaningful share of code sits in hard-to-follow functions.
CXI.D: Many hard functions or a heavy tail of very complex ones.
CXI.E: Most code lives in very complex functions; refactor before extending.

COI.A: Dependency structure is layered, acyclic and well spread.
COI.B: Healthy structure with minor cycles or hubs.
COI.C: Noticeable cycles, wide fan-out or hubs; changes ripple.
COI.D: Tangled dependencies; cycles and hubs dominate the graph.
COI.E: Pervasive cycles and hubs; modules cannot change independently.

OEI.B: A few abstractions without clear payoff (heuristic).
OEI.D: Much indirection that is not paid for by use (heuristic).

MAI.A: SIG-style profile is excellent: small units, low branching, little duplication.
MAI.B: Good maintainability profile with some larger units.
MAI.C: Average maintainability; size, branching or duplication need attention.
MAI.D: Below average; large or complex units and/or duplication are common.
MAI.E: Poor maintainability profile across most sub-ratings.
